preamble: Prothesis of [a] adds a vowel at the start of a word. A well-documented areal case is the avoidance of word-initial /r/ in Basque, Gascon and parts of Sardinia, where Latin or Romance words beginning with r- acquired a prothetic a- (Latin rosa > Basque arrosa, Latin rota > Gascon arròda).

examples.note: Basque does not allow word-initial r; borrowed r- words receive a prothetic vowel, here a-.
Gascon regularly adds a- before Latin initial r- (also arrat 'rat'); ròda is an alternative form. The change is often attributed to the Basque substrate.
